partners.mechanism_chain: ECM1 (HGNC:27979) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Skin thickening (HP:0000951); APOA1 (HGNC:554) —DISRUPTS→ Amyloid fibril formation (GO:0002026); Amyloid fibril formation (GO:0002026) —LEADS_TO→ Systemic amyloidosis (HP:0003257). Loss-of-function mutations in ECM1 disrupt extracellular matrix organization leading to phenotypes like skin thickening in lipoid proteinosis. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in APOA1 disrupt the normal process of amyloid fibril formation, leading to systemic amyloidosis. The convergence occurs at the level of protein homeostasis and extracellular matrix integrity, where dysregulation in either pathway can lead to aberrant protein deposition and tissue dysfunction.

partners.mechanism_chain: ECM1 (HGNC:2730) —DISRUPTS→ extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ skin thickening and hoarseness (HP:0001348); ITGA2B (HGNC:6033) —DISRUPTS→ platelet activation (GO:0007599); platelet activation (GO:0007599) —LEADS_TO→ bleeding (HP:00114152); platelet activation (GO:0007599) —LEADS_TO→ abnormal platelet aggregation (HP:0001876). Loss-of-function mutations in ECM1 cause lipoid proteinosis, leading to amorphous hyaline material deposition in the skin and associated fragility and bruising.
